newsitem.title: USA: Former St. Louis, Mo., comptroller leaves prison.
newsitem.headline: Former St. Louis, Mo., comptroller leaves prison.

text.p: Former St. Louis Comptroller Virvus Jones spent his first night out of federal prison Thursday in a St. Louis halfway house.
Donald Wolff, Jones' attorney, said Friday that Jones was released from a federal prison in Millington, Tenn., after serving about 10 months of his one year and one day sentence.
Jones pleaded guilty in September 1995 to two felony counts of income tax fraud, including failing to disclose he used campaign funds for personal use.
Wolff said Jones is scheduled to remain in the halfway house for the next two months, although Jones could be subject to a period of supervised release.
"He's doing very well," Wolff said. "He has a good attitude."

Jones was indicted in April 1995 along with Craig Walker, a former managing director of public finance at Prudential Securities Inc, and four others, according to the U.S. Attorney's Office in St. Louis.

The six had been charged with conspiring to hand Jones a victory in the 1993 Democratic primary race for St. Louis comptroller by secretly backing Penny Alcott, one of the individuals indicted, as a stalking horse candidate.
According to the U.S. Attorney's office, everyone but Walker entered guilty pleas.
In December, Walker was found guilty of conspiring to defraud the city of St. Louis and its voters, mail fraud, and obstruction of justice.
In March, he was sentenced to 33 months in prison on each count with the sentence running concurrently.
